quickAnswer: Pick Lower Düden for a dramatic 40-metre cliff-to-sea drop viewed from Lara’s park or a Kaleiçi boat, Upper Düden for a shaded cave walk behind the curtain of water, Kurşunlu for pine-forest calm paired with Perge, and Manavgat only if you are already driving east toward Side or Alanya.

body.text: How do Upper Düden, Lower Düden (cliff-to-sea) and Kurşunlu waterfalls differ?

Upper Düden (Kepez) is a compact park where you walk through a damp rock cave behind the falls; Lower Düden (Karpuzkaldıran, Lara) plunges 40 metres straight off coastal cliffs into the Mediterranean; and Kurşunlu (Aksu) drops 18 metres through a shaded two-kilometre pine canyon linking seven emerald ponds.

body.text: Which waterfall is best seen by boat from Kaleiçi harbour?

Lower Düden (Karpuzkaldıran) is the only Antalya waterfall directly visible from the sea, making it the signature highlight of two-hour and half-day boat trips departing Kaleiçi Old Harbour. Viewing the 40-metre cascade from deck level captures the full travertine cliff face and constant mist rainbows that clifftop terraces partially hide.

If you prefer staying ashore, Lower Düden’s clifftop park in Lara is free, open 24 hours, and takes just 20–30 minutes to stroll. Morning boats from Kaleiçi Marina generally encounter calmer seas and clearer eastward light on the cliff wall than windy late-afternoon sailings.
How do you pair Kurşunlu with Perge or Aspendos?

Visit Perge Ancient City first at 08:30 while the wide Roman colonnaded street is cool, drive 15 minutes north to Kurşunlu Waterfall Nature Park for shaded late-morning walking and lunch, and finish at Aspendos Roman Theatre in the mid-afternoon before returning along the D400 to Antalya.

Both ancient sites sit along the same eastern corridor described by [Turkish Museums](https://turkishmuseums.com/blog/detail/5-must-see-ancient-cities-in-antalya/10055/4). Official 2026 Ministry of Culture and Tourism e-ticket rates via [muze.gov.tr](https://muze.gov.tr/ETicket) are €11 for Perge and €15 for Aspendos. Adding Manavgat Waterfall only makes logistical sense if you are staying in Side or continuing east toward Alanya, as its wide four-metre river drop does not justify a separate 150-kilometre round trip from central Antalya.
Which waterfall is easiest with strollers or seniors?

Lower Düden’s Düden Park in Lara is by far the easiest option for strollers, wheelchairs, and seniors because its paved coastal walkways are flat, wide, and step-free from parking to the cliff-edge viewpoints. Manavgat Waterfall ranks second, offering level viewing decks and riverside tea gardens just steps from its car park.
Keep this practical waterfall checklist in mind before setting out:

items: Skip the Upper Düden cave passage if anyone in your group struggles with slippery stone steps or low rock ceilings.
Wear rubber-soled shoes at Kurşunlu; pine needles and spray make stone paths slick around the seven ponds.
Visit Kurşunlu on weekday mornings to avoid weekend Antalya family picnic traffic.
Bring a light windbreaker on Kaleiçi harbour boats when cruising close to Lower Düden’s spray.
Check seasonal closing times (Kurşunlu typically closes around 17:30–18:00 in winter) before planning a late-afternoon stop.

faq.q: Can you swim at Düden, Kurşunlu, or Manavgat waterfalls?
faq.a: Swimming is not permitted inside Upper Düden or Kurşunlu Nature Park, and Lower Düden drops directly into deep open sea off steep cliffs. Some Kaleiçi boat tours anchor safely offshore nearby for a Mediterranean swim stop.

faq.q: Is there an entrance fee for Lower Düden Waterfall?
faq.a: No. Viewing Lower Düden from Düden Park along the Lara clifftop is free and open year-round. Upper Düden, Kurşunlu Nature Park, and Manavgat Waterfall charge modest on-site municipal or park entry fees.

faq.q: How long do you need at Kurşunlu Waterfall Nature Park?
faq.a: Allow 60 to 90 minutes to walk the main loop past the 18-metre waterfall, stone footbridges, and seven interconnected ponds, plus extra time if stopping for tea or lunch under the pines.

faq.q: Can you reach Kurşunlu Waterfall by public transport from Antalya?
faq.a: Yes. Local municipal buses and Aksu minibuses (including lines serving Kurşunlu from Antalya’s bus terminal) run to the park, though combining Kurşunlu with Perge and Aspendos is much faster by rental car or private driver.

faq.q: Which Antalya waterfall is best in late summer when rainfall is low?
faq.a: Lower Düden and Manavgat maintain strong, reliable water volume throughout August and September because they are fed by major karst river systems rather than purely seasonal mountain streams.

faq.q: Is Upper Düden worth visiting if you already saw Lower Düden?
faq.a: Yes, if you enjoy shaded gardens and walking through the cool cave behind the cascade. They are completely different settings on the same river system, separated by roughly 25–30 minutes in city traffic.
